title: MNBL generation attempt state
description: Persisted after every transition by worldbridge::schedule (canonical JSON, atomically replaced). Seeds follow mnbl.retry-seed/1: attempt 0 uses masterSeed; attempt k >= 1 uses, for counter c = 0, 1, ..., the first four bytes (big-endian uint32) of SHA-256('mnbl.retry-seed/1' 0x00 BE32(masterSeed) BE32(k) BE32(c)), keeping the first value no earlier attempt used (derivationCounter = c). Only failures whose every reason code is in the world-quality policy's retryableQualityCodes are retried; input, mechanical, parser and engine failures end the generation. A cancelled attempt resumes with its own seed; accepted, exhausted and failed states are final and never regenerated. Exhaustion keeps every reason and never substitutes Calradia. One process drives a state at a time (exclusive <state>.lock); each write is flushed and renamed over the state with write-through. A loaded state must re-derive every seed, keep every attempt before the last as a rejection, and agree with the request it is resumed for (requestId, configurationId, campaignInstanceId, masterSeed, maxAttempts). Attempt work lives in <work>/<first 16 hex of requestId>/attempt-<index>-run-<run>, created exclusively: an existing directory is a work collision, never adopted.

canonicalJson.description: The state file is the RFC 8785 canonical form plus a final newline.

runs.description: Times this attempt was started (a cancelled attempt resumes as another run with the same seed).

history.description: Earlier runs of this attempt, oldest first: the record a run had when it was interrupted (state 'running' after a hard kill or work collision, 'cancelled' after cancellation).
